question: AR Rehman, Gulzar and _____ won the 52nd annual Grammy Award for the best motion picture song ‘Jai ho’.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tanvi Shah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards (2010), the song "Jai Ho" from the film *Slumdog Millionaire* won the award for Best Song Written for Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media. (जय हो गीत — ग्रैमी पुरस्कार)

 

• The award was jointly given to composer A.R. Rahman, lyricist Gulzar, and singer Tanvi Shah, who wrote and performed the additional rap verse in the song.

 

• This made Tanvi Shah the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award.

 

• A.R. Rahman also won a second Grammy that year, for Best Compilation Soundtrack Album for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media, for the *Slumdog Millionaire* soundtrack.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• *Slumdog Millionaire* (2008), directed by Danny Boyle, also won the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Original Song for "Jai Ho" in 2009, shared by A.R. Rahman and Gulzar.

 

• Dev Patel and Freida Pinto played the lead roles of Jamal and Latika in the film but were not part of the music award.

 

NOTE

 

• Danny Boyle (Option 1): He directed *Slumdog Millionaire* but had no role in composing/writing the song "Jai Ho".

 

• Dev Patel (Option 3): He played the male lead, Jamal Malik, in the film; not connected to the Grammy for the song.

 

• Freida Pinto (Option 4): She played the female lead, Latika, in the film; not connected to the Grammy for the song.

question: Raziya Sultan was the first and only female ruler of the Sultanate, who ascended the throne in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1236 AD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raziya Sultan (Raziya-ud-Din) was the daughter of Iltutmish of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty and ascended the throne of the Delhi Sultanate in 1236 AD. (रज़िया सुल्तान — 1236 ई.)

 

• She was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, reigning until 1240 AD.

 

• She was nominated as successor by her father Iltutmish over his sons, but nobles initially placed his son Rukn-ud-din Firuz on the throne before Raziya overthrew him and took power herself in 1236.

 

• She faced opposition from Turkish nobles partly because of her gender and her closeness to the Abyssinian noble Malik Yaqut; she was eventually defeated and killed in 1240 AD.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty (1206-1290) was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak; other notable rulers include Iltutmish, Balban, and Nasir-ud-din Mahmud.

 

• Raziya is known to have dressed in male attire and led her armies personally, breaking with the purdah norms of the time.

 

NOTE

 

• 1238 AD (Option 1): No significant event marks Raziya's accession in this year; she was already ruling by this time.

 

• 1241 AD (Option 3): By this year Raziya had already been deposed and killed (1240); this postdates her actual reign.

 

• 1242 AD (Option 4): This is after Raziya's death in 1240 and does not correspond to her accession.

question: By which National Waterways (NW) of India, are the delta channels of Mahanadi and Brahmani rivers and East Coast Canal connected?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NW 5.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Waterway 5 (NW5) covers the Brahmani-Kharsua-Dhamra rivers, the Mahanadi delta river system, and the East Coast Canal (Charbatia-Dhamra stretch) in Odisha. (राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग 5 — ओडिशा)

 

• It stretches for about 588 km and connects the delta channels of the Mahanadi and Brahmani rivers with the East Coast Canal, linking Paradip, Dhamra and other points along the Odisha coast.

 

• Note the distinction between the Brahmani river (Odisha, part of NW5) and the Brahmaputra river (Assam, part of NW2) — the two are commonly confused.

 

• National Waterways were expanded under the National Waterways Act, 2016, which designated 111 waterways as National Waterways, while NW1 to NW5 had been declared earlier under separate Acts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NW1: Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system (Prayagraj-Haldia).

 

• NW3: West Coast Canal along with the Champakara and Udyogmandal Canals, Kerala.

 

NOTE

 

• NW 1 (Option 1): This is the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, not related to Odisha's Mahanadi/Brahmani deltas.

 

• NW 3 (Option 2): This refers to the West Coast Canal in Kerala, unrelated to Odisha.

 

• NW 2 (Option 3): This is the Brahmaputra waterway in Assam, a different river system from the one described.

question: The Working Group under the chairmanship of __________ in the year_________ proposed a new intermediate monetary aggregate to be referred to as NM2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. YV Reddy; 1998.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Working Group on Money Supply: Analytics and Methodology of Compilation, chaired by Dr. Y.V. Reddy, submitted its report in 1998. (मुद्रा आपूर्ति कार्य समूह — डॉ. वाई.वी. रेड्डी, 1998)

 

• This working group introduced new monetary aggregates — NM1, NM2, NM3 — replacing the earlier M1, M2, M3, M4 classification used by the RBI, along with new liquidity aggregates L1, L2, L3.

 

• NM2 comprises NM1 plus short-term time deposits of residents (up to and including a contractual maturity of one year) with the banking system.

 

• Dr. Y.V. Reddy later went on to become the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (2003-2008).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI adopted the new monetary and liquidity aggregates recommended by this Working Group with effect from 1999-2000.

 

• NM3, the broadest of the new monetary aggregates, is analogous to the old M3.

 

NOTE

 

• Dr. C Rangarajan; 1996 (Option 1): Dr. Rangarajan was RBI Governor from 1992-1997 but did not chair this specific working group on the NM2 aggregate.

 

• Dr. KV Kamath; 1995 (Option 3): Dr. Kamath is a noted banker (ICICI Bank, NDB) but was not associated with this RBI working group.

 

• Dr. PK Mohanty; 1998 (Option 4): Not the chairman of this working group; incorrect person named.

question: In which state of India is the Tadoba National Park located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tadoba National Park, along with the adjoining Andhari Wildlife Sanctuary, forms the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve (TATR), located in Chandrapur district of Maharashtra. (ताडोबा राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — महाराष्ट्र)

 

• It is Maharashtra's oldest and largest national park, established in 1955, and is one of India's premier Project Tiger reserves.

 

• The park is named after the local deity "Tadoba" (a Gond tribal god) and the Tadoba Lake.

 

• It is known for its Bengal tiger population and dense teak and bamboo forests.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major tiger reserves in Maharashtra include Melghat, Pench, Sahyadri, Bor, and Nawegaon-Nagzira.

 

• Project Tiger was launched in 1973 and currently covers over 50 tiger reserves across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Home to the Gir National Park (Asiatic lions), not Tadoba.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Home to tiger reserves like Kanha, Bandhavgarh, and Panna, but Tadoba itself is in Maharashtra.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Home to Periyar Tiger Reserve, not Tadoba.

question: Which fundamental duty applies to you when you see your college friends start fighting with the canteen person when he passed a few anti-religious statements?
option_1: To promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood
option_2: To value and preserve the rich heritage
option_3: To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry
option_4: To protect and improve our natural environment
solution_text:
The correct answer is To promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(e) of the Indian Constitution lists the fundamental duty "to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities." (मौलिक कर्तव्य — सद्भाव और भाईचारा)

 

• The scenario in the question — friends fighting with the canteen worker after he made anti-religious statements — directly concerns maintaining communal/religious harmony, which is exactly what this duty addresses.

 

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are listed in Part IVA (Article 51A).

 

• Originally 10 duties were added; an 11th duty (regarding parents providing education to children) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be directly enforced by courts.

 

NOTE

 

• To value and preserve the rich heritage (Option 2): This is Article 51A(f), concerning composite culture, not communal conduct.

 

• To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry (Option 3): This is Article 51A(h), about rational and scientific thinking, not communal harmony.

 

• To protect and improve our natural environment (Option 4): This is Article 51A(g), concerning the environment and wildlife, unrelated to this scenario.

question: When was the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1920.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was established on 31 October 1920 in Mumbai (Bombay), making it the oldest trade union federation in India. (अखिल भारतीय ट्रेड यूनियन कांग्रेस — 1920)

 

• Its founding president was Lala Lajpat Rai, and it was founded with support from leaders like Joseph Baptista, N.M. Joshi, and Diwan Chaman Lall.

 

• AITUC played a key role in advocating for labour rights during the colonial period and became affiliated with the Communist Party of India after India's independence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• N.M. Joshi served as the general secretary of AITUC for many years and represented Indian labour at the International Labour Organisation (ILO).

 

• Other major trade union federations in India include INTUC (1947) and BMS, the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (1955).

 

NOTE

 

• 1926 (Option 1), 1924 (Option 2) and 1928 (Option 3): These years are incorrect; AITUC was founded in 1920, not in any of these later years.

question: Who founded the Arya Samaj in Mumbai in 1875?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami Dayanand Saraswati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay (Mumbai) on 10 April 1875. (आर्य समाज — स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती)

 

• He propagated the philosophy of "Back to the Vedas" and rejected idol worship, caste discrimination, and superstitions, advocating a return to Vedic principles.

 

• He is also known for authoring "Satyarth Prakash", a key text laying out Arya Samaj's principles.

 

• The Arya Samaj later established institutions like Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) schools and colleges across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Swami Dayanand Saraswati's birth name was Mool Shankar; he was born in Tankara, Gujarat.

 

• The Arya Samaj later became especially influential in Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Debendranath Tagore (Option 2): He led the Brahmo Samaj (as its main reformer after Raja Ram Mohan Roy), not the Arya Samaj.

 

• Swami Vivekanand (Option 3): He founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, not the Arya Samaj.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Option 4): He founded the Brahmo Sabha (later Brahmo Samaj) in 1828, not the Arya Samaj.

question: By which of the following methods do red algae reproduce?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fragmentation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Red algae (Rhodophyta) commonly reproduce vegetatively through fragmentation, where a broken piece (fragment) of the thallus grows into a new independent organism. (लाल शैवाल — विखंडन द्वारा प्रजनन)

 

• Besides fragmentation, red algae also reproduce asexually (via non-motile spores) and sexually, since red algae characteristically lack flagellated/motile stages at any point in their life cycle.

 

• Red algae get their colour from the pigment phycoerythrin, in addition to chlorophyll, and are mostly marine, found at greater depths than most other algae.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of red algae include Porphyra, Gracilaria, and Gelidium — the latter two are commercially important sources of agar and carrageenan.

 

• Fragmentation is also a common mode of vegetative reproduction in other simple organisms like Spirogyra and fungi.

 

NOTE

 

• Grafting (Option 1): An artificial method of vegetative propagation used in flowering plants (e.g., fruit trees), not applicable to algae.

 

• Cutting (Option 2): An artificial propagation technique used for higher plants like roses and sugarcane, not characteristic of red algae.

 

• Micropropagation (Option 3): A tissue-culture based technique used to clone plants in laboratories, not a natural reproductive method of red algae.

question: Who is called the father of Local Self-Government in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Ripon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Ripon, Viceroy of India from 1880-1884, is known as the "Father of Local Self-Government in India". (स्थानीय स्वशासन के जनक — लॉर्ड रिपन)

 

• He issued the famous Resolution on Local Self-Government in 1882, which promoted the establishment of local bodies like municipalities and district boards with elected representatives.

 

• He is also known for repealing the Vernacular Press Act (1878) and for attempting to pass the Ilbert Bill (1883), which sought judicial equality for Indian judges.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Ripon's local self-government reforms laid the foundation for later developments such as the Government of India Act, 1919, which introduced dyarchy and further devolved powers locally.

 

• The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts (1992) later gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and municipalities respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 1): Known for introducing the Permanent Settlement (1793) in Bengal and civil service reforms, not local self-government.

 

• Lord Wellesley (Option 2): Known for the Subsidiary Alliance System, not local self-government.

 

• Lord William Bentinck (Option 4): Known for social reforms like the abolition of Sati (1829) and introducing English education, not local self-government.

question: Which of the following is NOT a physical change?
option_1: Heating of iron rod to red hot
solution_text:
The correct answer is Curdling of milk.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A physical change is one in which no new substance is formed and the change is usually reversible, whereas a chemical change produces a new substance with different properties and is usually irreversible. (भौतिक और रासायनिक परिवर्तन)

 

• Curdling of milk involves the souring of milk due to bacterial action producing lactic acid, which denatures milk proteins (casein) — this forms a new substance and is a chemical change, not a physical one.

 

• Heating of an iron rod to red hot, evaporation of diesel, and sublimation of NH4Cl are all physical changes because no new substance is formed; the original substance can, in principle, be recovered by reversing the condition (cooling, condensation, or resolidifying respectively).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sublimation is the direct change of a solid to a gaseous state without passing through the liquid state; examples include camphor, naphthalene, iodine, and ammonium chloride (NH4Cl).

 

• Common chemical changes include rusting of iron, burning of fuel, digestion of food, and souring of milk.

 

NOTE

 

• Heating of iron rod to red hot (Option 1): A physical change — the iron only changes temperature/glow, no new substance forms.

 

• Evaporation of diesel (Option 3): A physical change — diesel merely changes from liquid to vapour state.

 

• Sublimation of NH4Cl (Option 4): A physical change — NH4Cl changes directly from solid to gas and can be resolidified without any change in chemical composition.

question: Who among the following Indian cricketers were named the Wisden’s cricketer of the year in the 2022 edition of the Almanack?
option_1: Surya Kumar Yadav and Axar Patel
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohit Sharma and Jasprit Bumrah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Wisden Cricketers' Almanack 2022 edition, Rohit Sharma and Jasprit Bumrah were named among the "Five Cricketers of the Year". (विजडन क्रिकेटर ऑफ द ईयर 2022 — रोहित शर्मा और जसप्रीत बुमराह)

 

• The Wisden Cricketers' Almanack, first published in 1864 by John Wisden, is often called the "Bible of Cricket" and is published annually in England.

 

• The "Five Cricketers of the Year" is one of Wisden's oldest honours (since 1889); once named, a cricketer cannot receive the honour again.

 

• Rohit Sharma and Jasprit Bumrah were recognised for their consistent performances for India across formats.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wisden also separately names the "Leading Cricketer in the World" and the "Leading T20 Cricketer in the World" each year.

 

• Previous Indian recipients of the Cricketer of the Year honour include Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli, and Ravindra Jadeja, among others.

 

NOTE

 

• Surya Kumar Yadav and Axar Patel (Option 1): Not named among Wisden's Cricketers of the Year in the 2022 Almanack.

 

• Virat Kohli and Bhuvneshwar Kumar (Option 2): Virat Kohli had already received this honour in an earlier edition (2018); this pairing was not named in 2022.

 

• Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli (Option 4): Only Rohit Sharma (along with Bumrah, not Kohli) was named in the 2022 edition.

question: Which of the following is responsible for the red colour of beetroot?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Betanin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Betanin is a red-violet pigment belonging to the class of betalains, responsible for the characteristic red/purple colour of beetroot. (बीटानिन — चुकंदर का लाल रंग)

 

• It is a glycosidic dye, obtained by combining betanidin with glucose, and is used commercially as a natural food colourant (E162).

 

• Beetroot is one of the richest natural sources of betalain pigments, which are found only in plants of the order Caryophyllales.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Curcumin is the yellow pigment found in turmeric.

 

• Beta carotene gives the orange colour to carrots, and lycopene gives the red colour to tomatoes and watermelon.

 

NOTE

 

• Curcumin (Option 1): The principal pigment of turmeric, giving it a yellow colour — unrelated to beetroot.

 

• Beta carotene (Option 3): Responsible for the orange colour in carrots and pumpkins, not the red of beetroot.

 

• Lycopene (Option 4): Responsible for the red colour in tomatoes and watermelon, not beetroot.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which group of Union Territories has the highest density of population?
option_1: Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu and Puducherry
option_2: Delhi, Chandigarh and Daman and Diu
option_4: Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu and Chandigarh
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, among Union Territories, Delhi (about 11,320 persons/sq km), Chandigarh (about 9,258 persons/sq km) and Puducherry (about 2,547 persons/sq km) recorded the highest population densities. (जनगणना 2011 — जनसंख्या घनत्व)

 

• Delhi had the highest population density among all Union Territories (and among all States/UTs in the country).

 

• Lakshadweep and Daman and Diu also had notably high densities, but lower than Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, Bihar was the most densely populated state in India, while Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest state density.

 

• India's overall population density in 2011 was about 382 persons per sq km.

 

NOTE

 

• Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu and Puducherry (Option 1): Excludes Delhi and Chandigarh, which have far higher densities than these three.

 

• Delhi, Chandigarh and Daman and Diu (Option 2): Daman and Diu's density is lower than Puducherry's; this combination is not the correct top three.

 

• Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu and Chandigarh (Option 4): Excludes Delhi, which has the highest density among all UTs.

question: Which Article deals with the election of the President?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 54.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 54 of the Indian Constitution deals with the "Election of President", specifying that the President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States. (अनुच्छेद 54 — राष्ट्रपति का निर्वाचन)

 

• The manner of election (by proportional representation through single transferable vote, and secret ballot) is detailed in Article 55.

 

• The President's term of office is covered in Article 56, and eligibility for re-election in Article 57.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 61 deals with the procedure for impeachment of the President.

 

• Article 52 simply states "There shall be a President of India," establishing the office itself.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 72 (Option 1): Deals with the President's pardoning power (pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, commutation of sentences).

 

• Article 74 (Option 3): Provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President.

 

• Article 66 (Option 4): Deals with the election of the Vice-President, not the President.

question: Identify an example of plasma as a state of matter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neon sign bulbs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plasma is often called the "fourth state of matter" — an ionised gas consisting of free electrons and positive ions, formed when a gas is subjected to very high energy. (प्लाज्मा — पदार्थ की चौथी अवस्था)

 

• Neon sign bulbs work by passing an electric current through neon gas at low pressure, which ionises the gas and produces a glowing plasma that emits characteristic coloured light.

 

• Other natural/artificial examples of plasma include the Sun and stars, lightning, the solar wind, the ionosphere, and fluorescent tube lights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three commonly known states of matter — solid, liquid, and gas — do not include plasma, which behaves distinctly due to its charged particles.

 

• Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) is sometimes referred to as a fifth state of matter, formed at temperatures close to absolute zero.

 

NOTE

 

• Blood (Option 1): "Blood plasma" is the liquid component of blood — a biological term, not the physics state-of-matter plasma; blood itself is not an example of plasma.

 

• Dry ice (Option 2): This is solid carbon dioxide (CO2), an example of the solid state, not plasma.

 

• Freon (Option 3): A group of chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) refrigerant gases, existing as ordinary gases/liquids, not plasma.

question: Classical Sarod player, Amjad Ali Khan was awarded ____________ in 2001 by the Government of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Vibhushan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, a renowned classical sarod player, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan — India's second-highest civilian award — in 2001. (पद्म विभूषण — अमजद अली खान)

 

• He belongs to the Bangash lineage / Senia Bangash school of sarod playing, a tradition spanning several generations of his family.

 

• Earlier in his career, he received the Padma Shri (1975) and the Padma Bhushan (1991).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are given in three categories in descending order of importance: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

 

• Amjad Ali Khan's sons, Amaan Ali Khan and Ayaan Ali Khan, are also accomplished sarod players carrying forward the family tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Bharat Ratna (Option 1): India's highest civilian award; Amjad Ali Khan has not been conferred this award.

 

• Padma Shri (Option 2): He received this earlier, in 1975, not in 2001.

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 4): He received this earlier, in 1991, not in 2001.

question: Which of the following statements is correct?
option_1: Pond water and sea water are considered as fresh water.
option_3: Rivers and sea water are considered as fresh water.
option_4: Rivers, creeks, lakes, ponds, and streams are all freshwater habitats.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rivers, creeks, lakes, ponds, and streams are all freshwater habitats.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Freshwater habitats are bodies of water with a low salt concentration (generally less than 1%), and include rivers, streams, creeks, lakes, ponds, and wetlands. (मीठे जल के आवास — नदियाँ, झीलें, तालाब)

 

• Sea water, in contrast, is saline/marine water with a high salt concentration and constitutes a distinct marine habitat, not a freshwater one.

 

• Freshwater ecosystems are broadly classified into lentic (still water, e.g. ponds, lakes) and lotic (flowing water, e.g. rivers, streams, creeks) habitats.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Freshwater ecosystems, though covering less than 1% of the Earth's surface, are home to a disproportionately large share of the world's biodiversity, including many fish species.

 

• Estuaries, where rivers meet the sea, are examples of brackish water habitats (a mix of fresh and salt water).

 

NOTE

 

• Pond water and sea water are considered as fresh water (Option 1): Incorrect — sea water is saline, not fresh.

 

• Sea water is freshwater habitat (Option 2): Incorrect — sea water is a marine/saline habitat.

 

• Rivers and sea water are considered as fresh water (Option 3): Incorrect — while rivers are freshwater, sea water is not.

question: Mahendravarman I who wrote Mattavilasa-prahasana is related to which of the following ruling dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pallava.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahendravarman I was a Pallava king (early 7th century CE) who authored the Sanskrit satirical play "Mattavilasa Prahasana" ("The Farce of Drunken Sport"). (महेंद्रवर्मन प्रथम — पल्लव वंश)

 

• He ruled from the Pallava capital of Kanchipuram and was a contemporary rival of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II.

 

• He was also a patron of rock-cut cave temple architecture, initiating the Pallava tradition of excavating cave temples.

 

• He held titles like "Vichitrachitta" and "Mattavilasa", reflecting his artistic and literary talents.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahendravarman I's son, Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla), defeated the Chalukyas and captured their capital Vatapi (Badami); he is also associated with the Mahabalipuram monuments.

 

• The Pallava dynasty ruled parts of South India from roughly the 3rd to 9th century CE, with Kanchipuram as their capital.

 

NOTE

 

• Maitraka (Option 1): A dynasty that ruled in Gujarat (Vallabhi) from the 5th-8th centuries CE, unrelated to Mahendravarman I.

 

• Pushyabhuti (Option 3): The dynasty of Harshavardhana in North India (Thanesar/Kannauj), unrelated to Mahendravarman I.

 

• Chalukya (Option 4): A rival dynasty of the Pallavas, based at Badami/Vatapi; Mahendravarman I fought against the Chalukyas but belonged to the Pallava dynasty himself.

question: Who is considered the highest law officer of the state in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Advocate general.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Advocate General is the highest law officer of a state in India, appointed by the Governor under Article 165 of the Constitution. (राज्य का महाधिवक्ता — एडवोकेट जनरल)

 

• The Advocate General must possess the qualifications required to be a judge of a High Court and advises the state government on legal matters, in addition to performing legal duties assigned by the Governor.

 

• The Advocate General holds office "during the pleasure of the Governor" and has the right to speak in and take part in proceedings of the State Legislature (without a vote).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The equivalent post at the Union (Central) level is the Attorney General of India, appointed under Article 76 by the President.

 

• The Advocate General's remuneration is decided by the Governor since it is not specified in the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Attorney general (Option 2): This is the highest law officer of the Union/Central government, not of a state.

 

• Chief justice of high court (Option 3): Heads the judiciary of the state's High Court, but is not designated as the state's "law officer" in the constitutional/legal sense.

 

• Auditor general (Option 4): There is no such standalone constitutional post by this exact name for states; audit functions are performed by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) at the national level.

question: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Bills is related to the provision of modifying the list of Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu?
option_2: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order Amendment Act, 2013
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2021 amended the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 to modify the list of Scheduled Castes in Tamil Nadu. (अनुसूचित जाति आदेश संशोधन विधेयक, 2021 — तमिलनाडु)

 

• The Bill provided for including "Devendrakula Velalar" as an umbrella term/synonym encompassing certain existing Scheduled Caste communities in Tamil Nadu, including Kudumban, Pallan, Pallar, and Devendrakulathan, among others.

 

• It was passed by both Houses of Parliament in 2021 and became the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Act, 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 are the principal instruments specifying which castes/tribes are recognised as SC/ST in each state, issued under Articles 341 and 342.

 

• Any change to the SC/ST lists requires an Act of Parliament; the lists cannot be altered by an executive/state notification alone.

 

NOTE

 

• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2019 (Option 1): This concerns modification to the Scheduled Tribes list, not Scheduled Castes.

 

• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order Amendment Act, 2013 (Option 2): This too concerns the Scheduled Tribes list, unrelated to the Tamil Nadu Scheduled Caste modification.

 

• The Constitution (Scheduled Caste) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2015 (Option 3): This year/version does not correspond to the actual Tamil Nadu Devendrakula Velalar amendment, which was enacted in 2021.

question: What is the primary benefit offered to businesses in Special Economic Zones (SEZs)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tax and duty concessions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are specially delineated duty-free enclaves treated as foreign territory for trade operations, duties and tariffs, primarily offering businesses tax and duty concessions to boost exports and investment. (विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र — कर एवं शुल्क में छूट)

 

• SEZ units in India enjoy benefits such as exemption from customs duties on imports/exports, income tax exemptions/holidays, and exemption from various other state/central levies.

 

• The SEZ Act, 2005 (effective 2006) governs the establishment, operation, and benefits of SEZs in India, aiming to promote exports, employment, and infrastructure development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's SEZ policy was first announced in 2000, evolving from the earlier Export Processing Zones (EPZs), the first of which was set up at Kandla, Gujarat, in 1965.

 

• SEZs are also expected to provide streamlined, single-window clearance for business approvals.

 

NOTE

 

• Guaranteed market share (Option 2): SEZs do not guarantee any specific market share to businesses operating within them.

 

• Mandatory government contracts (Option 3): There is no provision guaranteeing government contracts to SEZ businesses.

 

• Unlimited foreign investment (Option 4): While SEZs facilitate foreign investment, it is not "unlimited" or unregulated — it remains subject to India's FDI policy and sectoral caps.

question: Which of the following countries will host the ICC men’s Cricket World Cup in the year 2031?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India, Bangladesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2031 is scheduled to be jointly hosted by India and Bangladesh. (आईसीसी पुरुष क्रिकेट विश्व कप 2031 — भारत और बांग्लादेश)

 

• This will mark another instance of the ODI World Cup being held (partly or wholly) in India, following 1987, 1996, 2011, and 2023.

 

• The ICC announced its global events hosting rights cycle through 2031 as part of its Future Tours Programme (FTP) hosting allocations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 is scheduled to be co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka.

 

• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 is scheduled to be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia.

 

NOTE

 

• India, Sri Lanka (Option 2): This pairing corresponds to the hosts of the 2026 T20 World Cup, not the 2031 ODI World Cup.

 

• Sri Lanka and Pakistan (Option 3): This pairing is not the announced host combination for the 2031 World Cup.

 

• Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (Option 4): This pairing is not the announced host combination for the 2031 World Cup; India, not Sri Lanka, is the confirmed co-host.

question: By what name is the festival of Makar Sankranti celebrated in Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magh Bihu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Assam, the festival of Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Magh Bihu (also called Bhogali Bihu), marking the end of the harvesting season. (माघ बिहू — असम)

 

• It is celebrated in the Assamese month of Magh (mid-January), typically involving community feasts, bonfires (Meji), and traditional games.

 

• Magh Bihu is one of the three Bihu festivals of Assam, the other two being Rongali/Bohag Bihu (Assamese New Year, April) and Kati/Kongali Bihu (October).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Makar Sankranti is celebrated under various regional names across India: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Uttarayan (Gujarat), Lohri (Punjab, precedes it), and Khichdi (parts of North India).

 

• The festival marks the sun's transition into the Makara (Capricorn) zodiac and the start of its northward journey (Uttarayan).

 

NOTE

 

• Pedda Padunga (Option 1): Not a standard name for Makar Sankranti celebrations; not associated with Assam.

 

• Thai Pongal (Option 2): This is the Tamil name for Pongal, celebrated in Tamil Nadu, not Assam.

 

• Pongal (Option 3): The harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu, not Assam.

question: Which of the following terms is related to football?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bicycle Kick.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "Bicycle Kick" (also called an overhead kick or scissor kick) is a spectacular football (soccer) technique where a player kicks an airborne ball backwards, over their own head, while their body is horizontal/airborne. (बाइसिकल किक — फुटबॉल शब्द)

 

• It is considered one of the most athletic and visually striking skills in football, often used to score spectacular goals.

 

• Other common football terms include hat-trick, offside, free kick, corner kick, and nutmeg.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The bicycle kick is closely associated with football legends like Pelé and Cristiano Ronaldo, both known for scoring iconic goals using this technique.

 

• Football (soccer) is governed internationally by FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association).

 

NOTE

 

• Third man (Option 1): A fielding position in cricket, located behind the slips near the boundary.

 

• Overs (Option 3): A unit of measurement in cricket, referring to a set of six balls bowled.

 

• LBW, Leg Before Wicket (Option 4): A mode of dismissal in cricket, not a football term.
